NEVER git commit, never touch the main checkout, never run `uv`, never call a billed model, MCP indexing or the network, and never run `python -m bench run` or any script that calls a model (use grep/rg and file reads). FIRST run: [ -e .venv ] || ln -s /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv .venv ; then run tests as `PYTHONPATH=$PWD:$PWD/packages/worldkeeper/src TMPDIR=/tmp .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider <tests>` (PYTHONPATH must include $PWD/packages/worldkeeper/src, otherwise worldkeeper imports from the MAIN checkout). Ruff: `.venv/bin/python -m ruff check <py files>` and `-m ruff format <py files>`. Leave changes uncommitted. Work TESTS FIRST: write the new tests, run them, see them fail for the right reason, then make the change. You may update an existing test only if it pins the OLD behaviour this task deliberately changes; never weaken, skip or delete any other test.

ROLE: story-package editor plus test writer. You may edit ONLY: data/stories/continuity-initiative/knowledge.yaml (two `statement` lines), tests/test_richer_3a.py, tests/test_knowledge_projection.py, and any other test under tests/ that a failing test shows pins one of the two OLD statements (update only that pin). Do not touch handoffs.yaml, plot.md, storylets.md, storylet-routes.yaml, world.yaml, bench/ or any Python outside tests/.

THE CHANGE (wording supplied; do not invent replacements): in knowledge.yaml replace exactly two `statement` values, keeping each entry's quoting style, and nothing else in the entries:
1. entry `k_sl_3a_a_r1`, `statement` (currently `'Kristin reaches Michelle alive, and the two share one unhurried moment before Michelle returns to directing prisoners through stolen radios and coded announcements.'`) becomes: Kristin and Michelle have reunited. Michelle coordinates the prisoners through stolen radios and coded announcements.
2. entry `k_sl_3a_a_r2`, `statement` (currently `'Michelle shares one unhurried moment with Kristin, then explains that freeing this block means little without exposing the other sites.'`) becomes: Michelle has explained that freeing this block means little without exposing the other sites.
Do NOT change `delivery_text`, `must_convey`, `requires`, `establishes`, `action_evidence`, `earn_when`, aliases or any other field of these or any other entry. Both alternate realizations are projected from the same established facts, so both statements must change together.

TESTS (first, plain names; put them in tests/test_richer_3a.py, and projection ones in tests/test_knowledge_projection.py if they fit better there):
- The two statements equal the new text exactly; neither contains `unhurried`, `share`, `shares` or `reaches Michelle alive`; each is shorter than the old one (compare against the literal old lengths: old A-r1 = 164 characters, old A-r2 = 135 characters; compute them from the strings above).
- Everything else about A-r1 and A-r2 is unchanged: delivery_text, must_convey, requires, establishes, action_evidence, earn_when equal the literal current values read from the file BEFORE editing (compact literals).
- Projection: with `michelle_reached` and `uprising_prepared` true in 3A (use `_engine(true_facts=ARRIVED)`), the SCENE section of the projected narration prompt contains the NEW A-r1 statement and the NEW A-r2 statement (both realizations project from the same facts, see how tests/test_knowledge_projection.py or the speaker-line tests project established knowledge) and neither old statement. Per-speaker lines are still one per speaker per statement and limited to speakers present or named (reuse the checks in tests/test_speaker_lines.py; do not edit that file's existing tests).
- Grounding/reveal behaviour preserved: the earlier tests in tests/test_richer_3a.py that hand `Free the captives.` to k_sl_3a_a_r1 and `Ask Michelle about other sites.` (or the existing command) to k_sl_3a_a_r2 still pass unchanged.
- The prompt is shorter: build the 3A prompt (`ItemFactsProvider`, see tests/test_prompt_budget.py `_prompts` for how, with ARRIVED facts asserted) before and after in the same test run by monkeypatching nothing: instead assert that the SCENE text of the new prompt is shorter than a literal-old-statement reconstruction of the same text (replace the new statements by the old ones in the prompt string and compare lengths).
Then run: tests/test_richer_3a.py tests/test_knowledge_projection.py tests/test_speaker_lines.py tests/test_prompt_budget.py tests/test_prompt_presence.py tests/test_prompt_inert_lines.py tests/test_markdown_story_package.py tests/test_package_audit.py tests/test_scene_roleplay_contract.py tests/test_knowledge_leakage_matrix.py tests/test_speaker_presence.py tests/test_spine_expected_reveals.py tests/test_3ab_spine_prompts.py tests/test_3a_records_followup.py tests/test_late_scene_repro.py tests/test_discovery_continuity.py, plus every test file whose grep for the two old statements matched.

FINAL MESSAGE: the two one-line diffs, every test changed or added, and the old/new statement lengths.

ROLE: bench harness engineer. You may edit/create ONLY: bench/frozen_prompts.py (new), tests/test_frozen_prompts.py (new). Do not edit any other file.

PURPOSE: a saved-prompt diagnostic needs the narrator prompt of scene 3A at later commands (c4 = "Enter the medical level.", c5 = "Ask Michelle about the lemon cake.", and later c6-c9) for the CURRENT story, WITHOUT a model call, and then needs to send exactly that saved payload N times. `bench prompt` only builds fresh-entry prompts, so build a faithful OFFLINE PREFIX by scripting the earlier commands through the real engine, as tests/test_richer_3a.py does (read its `_engine`, `_handoff`, `_authored_provider` helpers and the command-to-reveal table near `(ARRIVED, "Enter the medical level.", "k_sl_3a_b_r2")`; the command to reveal map for the nine commands is: Free the captives. -> k_sl_3a_a_r1; Read the wrist tags. -> k_sl_3a_f_r1; Listen to the stolen radio. -> k_sl_3a_g_r1; Enter the medical level. -> k_sl_3a_b_r2; Ask Michelle about the lemon cake. -> k_sl_3a_h_r1; Ask the senior official about the gate codes. -> its entry in that table (find it); Check the checkpoint reader. -> k_sl_3a_i_r1 or the table's entry; Tell the prisoners to start the uprising at the checkpoints. -> k_sl_3a_c_r1 or the table's entry; Lead the prisoners upward toward the command levels. -> the table's entry/transition. Read the table and use ITS ids, not mine, wherever they differ).

BUILD, in bench/frozen_prompts.py (importable as `bench.frozen_prompts`, plus `python -m bench.frozen_prompts capture ...` and `... replay ...` CLI entry points with argparse):
1. `capture(variation_path, endpoints, out_path)` where endpoints is a list of 1-based command numbers (e.g. [4, 5]) of the script in the variation (`variation["scripts"]["3A"][0]["inputs"]`; load the variation with `bench.core.load_variation`, seed the entry state with `bench.core.seeded_state_for_scene(variation, "3A")` so `thorough` entry state and `entry_facts` apply exactly as in the live runs). For each endpoint N: run commands 1..N-1 through `RuntimeEngine` using a scripted provider returning each command's authored delivery for its reveal (as `_authored_provider` in tests/test_richer_3a.py does), then build the exact WIRE PAYLOAD the real narration request for command N would send: use `bench.core`/`storygame.runtime.capture.build_capture_provider(state, mark_fixed=False)` (an ItemFactsProvider), and capture the dict passed to its `_send_http(wire_payload)` by patching `_send_http` on that instance to record payloads and return a canned valid reply (`json.dumps({"narration": json.dumps({"segments": [{"kind": "narration", "text": "Kristin acts."}], "selected_knowledge_ids": []})}).encode()`), calling `provider(command)` or the engine turn the way live runs do. Several HTTP calls may happen for one turn (e.g. a matcher call before the narration call); record ALL of them in order and mark the narration one (the one whose `system` is the narrator system prompt and whose user contains `CHARACTERS:`/`SCENE:`; identify it by structure, not a magic index). Write JSON: {"variation": name, "package_hash": ..., "endpoints": [{"n": N, "command": ..., "prefix": [commands 1..N-1], "committed_after_prefix": sorted true fact ids, "wire_payload": {...narration payload...}, "other_payloads": [...]}]}. Payload must be deterministic: capturing twice gives identical JSON.
2. `replay(frozen_path, samples, out_path, *, send=None)`: for each endpoint and each sample 1..samples, POST the saved `wire_payload` exactly as saved through the SAME transport the provider uses (construct the provider as in capture and call its `_send_http`; `send` is an injectable callable for tests, default is the provider's real `_send_http` after `bench.core.load_dotenv()`); one request per sample; no retries; catch exceptions per sample and KEEP them; never replace a failed sample. After each sample append {"n","sample","command","narration" (decoded narration string, or raw body if undecodable),"error","raw"} to out_path (rewrite the whole JSON list each time so a crash keeps partial results). Print `n sample ok|error` per sample. Do not decode into engine state; this is a prompt replay only.
3. A `--dry-run` for replay that prints the request count and endpoints and sends nothing.

TESTS (first; tests/test_frozen_prompts.py; offline only; tests must not touch the network nor read .env; monkeypatch `urlopen`/`_send_http`; keep each test fast):
- Capture endpoints [4, 5] on the checked-in variation `bench/variations/richer-3a-c.json`: both payloads exist, are deterministic across two captures, `committed_after_prefix` for c4 contains michelle_reached, wrist_tags_read, radio_loop_known (use the fact ids the table/NEW_FACTS uses) and for c5 also the medical fact established by `k_sl_3a_b_r2`; the c4 user prompt contains `Enter the medical level.` and the current A-r1 statement from knowledge.yaml; the c5 user prompt contains the medical statement.
- Capturing from two different packages differ only where the packages differ: `bench/variations/richer-3a-c-control.json` vs `richer-3a-c.json` at endpoint 4 give user prompts whose line-level diff contains the changed A-r1 delivery wording / frame lines and no unrelated drift (assert the diff is non-empty and every differing line mentions Michelle, the reunion or the uprising wording; or simply assert the two payloads differ and the system prompts are equal).
- Replay: with an injected `send` returning a canned reply, `samples=3` over two endpoints makes exactly 6 calls, records each, keeps a raising sample as an error entry without retrying or replacing it, the saved wire payload is passed unmodified, and `--dry-run` sends nothing.
- A sanity test that the captured c4/c5 user prompt lengths are within 40% of the recorded run4 lengths (3275 and 3706 characters, maxima from bench/results/richer-3a-probe/candidate-run4 which may be absent in CI: skip that one test if the directory is missing).
Run: tests/test_frozen_prompts.py plus tests/test_bench.py tests/test_richer_3a.py. If a literal in this brief (a fact id, a command, a helper) does not exist, use what the repository has and say so in your final message; do not invent runtime features, and do not add retries or request-count shortcuts.

FINAL MESSAGE: the module's functions, the CLI usage lines, what the c4 and c5 payload user lengths are for richer-3a-c (compare with run4's 3275/3706), the list of other payloads per endpoint, and any limit of the offline prefix (e.g. item_facts differences from a live prefix).
